name: Cardiovascular disease
description: Heart failure with a recorded ejection fraction uses the MAGGIC risk score. Heart failure without one uses survival by age at diagnosis. A dated stroke uses survival after stroke by age. Other cardiovascular disease uses U.S. population mortality multiplied by published hazard ratios.

inputs.label: Coronary heart disease or prior myocardial infarction
Hospital stay for heart failure in the last 180 days
NYHA class (after a heart-failure hospital stay)
Taking an ACE inhibitor, ARB or ARNI

layers.label: Heart failure after a recent hospital stay: MAGGIC risk score
layers.description: MAGGIC risk score, applied after a heart failure hospital stay in the last 180 days. A missing NYHA class is set to IV, following a published validation of MAGGIC at hospital discharge (Michaels 2020). That study observed slightly more deaths than MAGGIC predicted.

layers.label: Heart failure: MAGGIC risk score
layers.description: MAGGIC integer risk score from 13 routine measurements. Published 1-year and 3-year mortality per score, from 39,372 patients in 30 studies (1980-2006). A Weibull curve extends survival past 3 years. Survival is capped at general population survival for the same age and sex. Missing measurements are averaged over the MAGGIC cohort. This widens the range.

layers.label: Heart failure: survival by age at diagnosis (UK cohort)
layers.description: Ejection fraction not found, so MAGGIC does not apply. Survival after a heart failure diagnosis by age at diagnosis, from 55,959 UK patients diagnosed 2000-2017. Applied relative to population survival, conditional on years since diagnosis. After 15 years (5 years if diagnosed at 95 or over), the last published excess mortality is applied.

layers.label: Stroke: survival by age at the stroke (U.S. Medicare)
layers.description: 5-year survival after acute ischaemic stroke by age group, from 1,019,267 U.S. Medicare patients aged 66 or over, admitted 2008-2012. Applied relative to population survival, conditional on years since the stroke. Share of deaths in the first 28 days: Shiga stroke register, Japan, 2011. Patients under 66 use the 66 to 74 curve. Haemorrhagic strokes use the same curves (5-year survival 55% against 59% for ischaemic strokes in the Shiga register). After 5 years, the year 1 to 5 excess mortality is applied. Other recorded conditions are not added, because the cohort already included them.

layers.label: Other cardiovascular disease x population mortality
layers.description: U.S. population mortality for age and sex, multiplied by the published all-cause mortality hazard ratio of each recorded condition: coronary disease, stroke, atrial fibrillation, peripheral artery disease, cardiomyopathy, diabetes. Ratios for several conditions are multiplied (Emerging Risk Factors Collaboration). Each ratio was measured on its own, so risk may be overstated when several conditions are present.

validation.dataset: UCI heart failure clinical records (Faisalabad, Pakistan, Ahmad et al. 2017)
validation.metric: Heart failure, MAGGIC layer: Harrell's C-index
validation.notes: Patient-level, predicted at enrolment from age, sex, ejection fraction, creatinine, smoking and diabetes; other inputs averaged. Assumes the record does not show the hospital stay.

validation.metric: Stroke: predicted 1-year survival
validation.notes: Published cohort, independent of the stroke layer's sources: predicted at admission (stroke layer), with ages spread evenly within each published quartile (median 77, IQR 66-85; ends 18 and 100 assumed) and the cohort's sex mix. Observed: 1-year all-cause mortality among patients with more than a year of follow-up.

validation.metric: Heart failure: MAGGIC-predicted 3-year mortality (published)
validation.notes: Published external validation of the MAGGIC score that this model's heart-failure layer reproduces at 1 and 3 years: MAGGIC underpredicted 3-year mortality here.
